newsitem.title: UK: Centrica document contains few surprises.
newsitem.headline: Centrica document contains few surprises.

text.p: Centrica's listing particulars, revealed on Friday, brought details of exceptional charges, but all in all unveiled little analysts did not already know.
"What we see is not surpising. A lot has been foreshadowed in the original demerger announcement and the meeting we had earlier this week," said one industry watcher.
Centrica will house British Gas' supply business and its Morecambe Bay gas field and is scheduled to be floated off next month.
British Gas said its 1996 fourth quarter results would contain exceptional charges for restructuring and contract talks.
The 341 million stg earmarked for the take-or-pay contract renegotiations was largely expected after British Gas announced early in December it had reached an agreement with British Petroleum.
British Gas also set aside 500 million stg for restructuring and cost cutting.

"This charge was not particularly expected, but it is not surprising because it is the last chance to make a big provision before the demerger," said another investment analyst, who also declined to be named.
"It is quite clear that there is a lot more cost-cutting planned," he added.
Trading in Centrica shares is expected to start on February 17, British Gas said in December.
